$comment: THE BROWSE DATABASE MANIFEST. This is the file behind 'are all the card and sealed databases
loading as expected', and adding a game or an artifact is a data edit here, never a code edit.
byteFloor values were MEASURED against production on 2026-09-20 and set to roughly 70% of the
observed Content-Length. That is loose enough to survive ordinary catalog growth and tight enough
to catch the failure that actually happens: a publish that truncates, or an empty file uploaded
over a good one. rowFloor is checked after parsing, where the shape allows it.
expect 400 is not a mistake. Pokemon's plaintext catalog is deliberately retired from the public
bucket (it is served as catalog.enc behind the catalog-key function), and Pokemon's neighbour
graph is pgvector rather than a file. Asserting the 400 is how we notice if either quietly
returns, which would be a data leak in the first case.

artifacts.why: Retired on purpose. A 200 here means the gated catalog leaked to anonymous callers.
